alex: Heads-up: reconcile-bot flagged 3 "shadow" configs in staging that don't exist in prod; looks like leftover GPU taints & a stray NetworkPolicy.
reconcile-bot: [ALERT] drift detected in namespace redwood-inference-staging: 3 resources (NetworkPolicy/gpu-isolation, ConfigMap/legacy-canary, PodDisruptionBudget/old-pdb)
jamie: can you paste the diff or run a quick `kubectl diff`?
suresh: quick link to the CI run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-drift/actions/runs/123456789 — plan shows removed vs desired.
alex: pasted snippet from `kubectl -n redwood-inference-staging get networkpolicy gpu-isolation -o yaml`:
```
metadata:
  name: gpu-isolation
  annotations:
    drift.redwood/ephemeral: "true"
  labels:
    app: gpu-provisioner
spec: ...
```
marta: that annotation pattern is from the old canary flow. We shouldn't open noisy PRs for those — prefer auto-prune for `drift.redwood/ephemeral=true` older than 7d.
jamie: agree but we need a safety net: do NOT auto-prune if label `redwood-lifecycle: managed` or ownerRef points to a Terraform-managed resource.
alex: proposal: add a GitOps CI job that runs nightly: (1) detect drift, (2) classify by annotation/age, (3) for ephemerals create an autodraft PR removing the resource, (4) post summary to #eng-infra. Canary removal only in staging, require 24h telemetry check before prod.
suresh: add an OPA gate so auto-prune only proceeds when `allow_auto_prune[true]` and GPU pool capacity delta < 5% to avoid accidental capacity churn.
marta: note: last week we saw ~4% idle GPU hours due to ghost nodePools from a misapplied helm patch. If pruning reduces reserved GPUs by 2 nodes that's ~\u0024 4.8k/mo — tagging cost team for review.
jamie: cost alert: we should auto-suggest the monthly savings in the PR template.
oper-bot: created issue #987: "staging-shadow-remediation-playbook" -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/987 :spiral_notepad:
alex: rough gate script I'm going to add to repo: 
```
# pseudo
if resource.annotations["drift.redwood/ephemeral"] == "true" and resource.age_days > 7 and not resource.labels["redwood-lifecycle"] == "managed":
  create_draft_pr(remove_resource)
else:
  annotate_for_manual_review
```
jamie: include terraform safeguards: snapshot TF state before any auto-prune: `terraform state pull > tfstate-<ts>.json` and attach to PR. Add `terraform import` detection for resources that Terraform knows about.
suresh: OPA snippet to block auto-prune if owner is terraform: `deny[msg] { input.labels["redwood-managed"] == "true"; msg = "managed by terraform" }`
marta: also add a Helm rollback playstep in the PR job: `helm rollback <rel> <rev>` and keep manifest backups in `gitops/backups/<timestamp>/`.
alex: On the monitoring side: watch gpu.util, kubeapi errors, and networkpolicy-deny counts for 2 hours after any canary prune. If anomalies, auto-create rollback PR.
jamie: I'm going to wire the PR template to auto-calc estimated savings and potential affected pods based on nodeSelector/gpu labels.
alex: pinging @oncall for visibility on the canary window tomorrow morning :bell:
oncall: noted — I'll be watching the canary window between 09:00-11:00 PT. If anything spikes I'll page.
jamie: quick command we used during triage: `kubectl get nodes -l accelerator=nvidia -o wide --show-labels` to map ghost requests to nodepools.
suresh: one more safety: require `manual_approve` if number_of_resources_to_prune > 5 or estimated_gpu_delta > 3 nodes.
marta: agreed. Also add a compact audit log entry in S3: `s3://ops-audit/drift-prs/<pr-number>.json` with diff and TF snapshot.
alex: I'll draft the PR for the CI job and the playbook text for the ops runbook. Leaving checklist in the issue. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
jamie: thanks — moving task to Sprint infra backlog and marking P0 for next deploy.
reconcile-bot: drift run complete — artifacts: https://ci.redwood.internal/drift/2150004321/artifacts
alex: closing loop — will post final playbook once PR is up.
